For eight vertices, verify.py independently reconstructs the rational 8-by-8 matrix, certifies \(QP=4DM\) coefficient-wise for all 64 entries (not finite sampling), verifies controlling polynomials \(9h^7F\) and \(-9hG\), exactly one positive root each with disjoint brackets, and confirms the other 60 entries remain strictly positive on \((0,9/2]\). Thus the claimed positivity set and end boundaries hold for the continuum of \(h\ge0\). Numerically displayed decimal approximations are nonessential. Remaining risks: mathematical reliance on the reproducible finite polynomial certificate and choice of model scope, not an unproved infinite sample.

originality.rationale: The precise claim is the all-size small-step behavior of UNWEIGHTED SYMMETRIC PATHS and the exact disconnected positivity interval for the first failing reversible path P8. A published general CTMC dimension-eight theorem covers the low-dimensional positive-side context and a different directed eight-state example; it does not determine the symmetric P8 interval or its algebraic roots. Earlier Padé examples use a unilateral shift; absolute-monotonicity theory has radius zero but does not imply this parameter-specific complete sign set. No statement logically implying the new sharp P8 classification was found in the inspected sources. Absence of an unseen equivalent specialization is not certified.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent path-specific calculation may be present in an unlocated or uninspected primary source, including unpublished work; searches and comparison do not establish historical uniqueness.
The subdiffusion preprint was not examined theorem-by-theorem; its distinct model makes exact implication implausible but this is an access/inspection limitation.
The positive interval for \(P_8\) is not generalized to arbitrary weighted graphs, higher paths, or Runge–Kutta internal stage positivity.

value.rationale: A unit-rate symmetric path is the canonical reversible discrete heat/Markov generator. Entrywise positivity is a discrete maximum-principle property of completed time integration. The precise first dimension where arbitrarily small timesteps fail, together with a full closed algebraic interval where nonnegativity returns and then fails again, rules out the naive monotonicity assumption that making the timestep smaller is always safe. The complete exact \(P_8\) classification is naturally motivated, nontrivial (64 rational entries with global sign analysis), and usable as a sharp benchmark for structure-preserving rational integrators, independent of a separate downstream theorem.
